items.title: Lay of the land: terrestrial conservation efforts cover a wider area than thought
items.summary: Governments around the world have pledged to conserve 30% of the terrestrial realm by 2030, but official data suggest that the target is barely halfway to being met. A combined global and national-level data set now shows that up to 27% of land area is conserved, but gaps in ecological representation remain.

items.title: Will my lack of country-specific grants limit my chances of employment abroad?
items.summary: A researcher in Latin America seeks advice on the best way to present themselves when applying for faculty positions in Europe and North America.

items.title: A guide to the Nature Index
items.summary: A description of the terminology and methodology used in this supplement, and a guide to the functionality that is available free online at natureindex.com.

items.title: Nature Index reveals the four countries to watch in biomedical engineering
items.summary: These nations are making their distinct mark in the field through specialization and collaboration.

items.title: Is this idea from AI or humans? A detector claims it can tell
items.summary: A tool called IdeaLens helps to judge whether concepts — rather than just writing — in scientific papers are AI-generated.

items.title: Some Jurassic period birds were flightless
items.summary: The fossil discovery of an early avian ancestor in China reveals that flightless birds lived alongside the known flying species.

items.title: Large blind test of methane-detecting satellites lends credibility to emissions data
items.summary: Twelve methane-sensing satellites were tested for their accuracy in measuring controlled-release events in the Arizona desert over a year-long blind test. Many were found to detect and quantify releases accurately, with instruments purpose-built for methane sensing performing best.

items.title: Daily briefing: China’s extraordinary rise in science
items.summary: Explore China’s efforts to grow its scientific and technological might. Plus, how butterflies trick the eye and what could be the oldest shipwreck ever found.

items.title: China’s AI research is booming: what it’s like to be on the front line
items.summary: China trains more AI talent than any other country. Nature spoke to analysts and scientists about how AI research there compares to the United States.

items.title: Protecting nature means valuing biodiversity
items.summary: Appeals for extra money are failing. Fundamental changes are needed to safeguard the planet for future generations.

items.title: ‘Incredible’: bleached corals thrive within days when touching healthy neighbour
items.summary: A coral fragment can form a tissue bridge with a dying counterpart — and provide it with crucial microalgae.

items.title: Alveolar stem cells go beyond making gas-exchange cells to repair damaged airways
items.summary: Alveolar type 2 (AT2) cells are the stem cells of the lung’s air sacs and are responsible for maintaining alveolar structure and gas exchange. A study that tracked AT2 cells shows that, after injury to the airway, they can also migrate between lung compartments and become bronchiolar cells to help repair damaged airways.

items.title: Hydrogels and MRI: meet three biomedical engineers reshaping health care
items.summary: Researchers are making great advances across medical disciplines, using a wide range of tools and processes.

items.title: How early tetrapods got their neck
items.summary: As fish evolved into four-limbed creatures, their skull separated from their shoulders to form a neck. Now we learn that this early neck was surprisingly rigid.

items.title: Structural basis of ligand recognition and gating in mosquito IRs
items.summary: Structural basis of ligand recognition and gating in mosquito IRs

items.title: Overlooked brown fat in our bodies linked to wide range of health benefits
items.summary: Massive study of more than 100,000 people finds surprise connection between ‘good’ body fat and improved mental health.

items.title: Smartwatch health data are piling up. How can doctors keep pace?
items.summary: To harness the full value of wearable devices for monitoring and diagnosing medical conditions, protocols must be established.

items.title: China’s extraordinary rise in science and how it will change the world
items.summary: The nation is on a trajectory to lead the world in science, a development that will reshape technological advancement, innovation and the balance of global power.

items.title: Evidence for multi-Li<sup>+</sup> clustering in lithium-ion battery electrolytes
items.summary: Machine-learning-enabled atomistic simulations, spectroscopy, electrochemical data and quantum-chemical calculations reveal previously unstudied multi-lithium-ion complexes without bound anions, improving understanding of lithium-ion-battery functionality at the atomic level.

items.title: Global conservation area coverage substantially exceeds current estimates
items.summary: A globally representative sample of 25 countries and territories indicates that conservation areas cover 26.81% of the land, much closer to the 30% by 2030 target than officially reported.

items.title: Engineered TYK2 dependence enables myeloid-selective IL-10 receptor agonism
items.summary: A tetravalent nanobody-based myeloid-selective IL-10 receptor agonist recapitulates IL-10’s potent suppression of monocytes, macrophages and dendritic cells while avoiding stimulation of T cells.

items.title: Elp1 is required for myeloid differentiation and brain repopulation
items.summary: Primary cultured haematopoietic stem and progenitor cells are used to analyse the molecular mechanisms of brain myeloid differentiation, and this platform enabled the identification of elongation factor ELP1 as an important regulator of this process.

items.title: Modelling mouse embryogenesis from chemically induced totipotent stem cells
items.summary: A mouse embryo model derived from chemically induced totipotent-like stem cells progresses through key developmental milestones, including gastrulation, embryonic axis formation, haematopoiesis and early organogenesis.

items.title: Competing mechanisms toughen bcc binary and medium-entropy alloys at 20 K
items.summary: The mechanical properties of medium-entropy alloys at 20 K show a plateau in tensile yield strength and fracture toughness as a function of temperature, with no apparent ductile-to-brittle transition.

items.title: Parity-dependent coupling of molecular spin chains to a superconductor
items.summary: Scanning tunnelling spectroscopy shows that the fractional spin-1/2 end states of molecular Haldane chains couple differently to a superconducting condensate depending on whether the chain contains an even or odd number of spin-1 triangulene units.

items.title: Capillary-selective vasodilation through myosin inhibition halts ischaemic cascades
items.summary: R(+)2501 reverses capillary no-reflow by relaxing pericytes, restoring microvascular perfusion and improving survival in animal models of myocardial infarction and acute kidney injury.

items.title: Evaluating space-based methane detection through a one-year blind test
items.summary: A year-long single-blind study shows that multiple satellites can accurately detect and quantify methane point-source emissions.

items.title: De novo design of cysteine proteases
items.summary: De novo-designed enzymes use an activated cysteine nucleophile to hydrolyse polypeptide backbones in a sequence-dependent manner.

items.title: Computational design of metalloproteases
items.summary: RFdiffusion methods are used to de novo design proteins with water-activating zinc-based active sites adjacent to a peptide substrate binding pocket, yielding highly active, programmable proteases with potential applications in therapeutics, biotechnology and bioremediation.

items.title: Divergent genomic evolution in astrocytomas and oligodendrogliomas
items.summary: Longitudinal genomic analyses in patients with astrocytoma or oligodendrioglioma suggest that these two types of tumour differ in the mechanisms by which they become resistant to treatment, with astrocytomas accumulating copy-number alterations and chromosomal instability markers but oligodendrogliomas acquiring new driver mutations.

items.title: Rh<sup>3+</sup> stabilized in KRh@MFI catalyses regioselective hydroformylation
items.summary: DFT investigations combined with spectroscopic and catalytic studies of disrupted subnanometric Rh2O3 clusters show that Rh+ centres in a zeolite-based catalyst are blocked with N-containing molecules, whereas Rh3+ sites are stabilized, allowing hydroformylation reactions with enhanced regioselectivity and efficiency.

items.title: Targeted stimulation of motor cortex ensembles drives learned movements
items.summary: Optogenetic stimulation of motor-cortex neuron ensembles shows that precisely timed activity in the primary motor cortex can generate learned neural patterns and movements, demonstrating an active role in skilled motor control.
